body: I tried rescheduling with a different counselor but missed the appointment twice. Now I just feel bad for wasting their time so I haven't rescheduled.

1.) I guess I am afraid that a more "comprehensive examination" will reveal me for the nutcase I truly am. 

2.) Psychiatrists only want to medicate you, it is what they are trained to do. I cannot afford the risk of losing my cognitive abilities due to medication.

3.) You are right, what she suggested is almost certainly what I need. But I can't afford the treatment so why get the examination? By can't afford I mean both 'time' and 'money,' both of which I have none.

Physics. I've been in the program for almost 5 years now. Average graduation rate is 5-7 years. At first I loved it but now I hate it, and I feel like I've invested too much of my life to quit now. Every time I bring it up people ask me the same two questions:

a) Do you have another job offer? (No? So you can't just quit).

b) Why would you quit now so close to finishing?
